title: Signal-driven Presets Lab: Safe Defaults, Explainable Trade-offs, and Simulation Panel
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype an interactive 'Signal-driven Presets Lab' within Redwood Console that helps engineers safely configure batching and prefix/KV caching. The lab surface combines: a) compact recommenders (safe defaults + why this choice), b) a simulation panel that replays a sample traffic slice to estimate cost/latency/accuracy impact, and c) an explainable guardrails composer that surfaces regression risk and an automatic rollback suggestion. Goal: move users from guesswork to predictable, explainable tuning with lightweight defaulting and one-click canary rollout integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype linked that demonstrates: 3 preset strategies (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) and a custom composer
Simulation panel shows token-saved, median-latency delta, and estimated cost per 1M requests for each preset
Guardrail composer lists 3 auto-checks (generation divergence, average latency spike, error-rate increase) with recommended thresholds and textual explanation
Microcopy and tooltip library created for each control explaining trade-offs in single-sentence form
Design tokens and component variants provided for dev handoff; annotated specs include accessibility contrast notes and keyboard flows
Canary/rollout CTA wires up to existing Rollouts surface (link to PR/issue) and includes quick rollback microcopy
comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Kicked off with research notes from ops runbook and telemetry team (see Confluence link). Primary insight: prefix cache has widely varying ROI by workload shape — need quick estimator.
2025-02-18 - Evan Rodriguez: Wireframes ready. Focused on making simulation inputs shallow (time window, request sample size) so it's fast and deterministic in the console.
2025-02-21 - Priya Anand (PM): Review feedback: Make 'why recommended' text explicit about quality regression risk and provide a preview toggle to show example responses under each preset.
2025-02-26 - Nate Kim (SRE): Implementation note: simulation will rely on anonymized traces from analytics; added dependency on ENG-80214 to expose a sample-export endpoint.
2025-02-28 - Accessibility review (Ana Lopez): Buttons and chip contrast validated; suggested adding aria-live region around simulation status updates for screen reader users.
2025-03-03 - Design review: Decision to compress guardrail composer into a two-column layout to preserve vertical space in small consoles. Need dev estimation update after handoff.
2025-03-04 - Evan Rodriguez: Updated prototype with canary CTA wired. Added rollback microcopy: 'Roll back to last stable preset in 1 click — no model change required.'
decisions: Use three named presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) instead of a numerical slider — helps communicate trade-offs clearly
Simulation will return three metrics (token savings, median latency delta, estimated monthly cost delta) to keep UI digestible
Guardrail checks are advisory by default but can be promoted to enforcement by enterprise customers via RBAC setting
Integrate with existing Rollouts surface (reuse routing toggles) rather than building a separate canary flow
Default preset for new projects: Balanced — provides modest savings without aggressive cache eviction policies
